Energy metrics for the winter M&V evaluation Since the Space_load and Misc_load values can be either negative or positive, it is helpful to consider their sign for interpretation of the results. Negative values correspond to heat loss when the enthalpy of the air stream is reduced (e.g., lower dry bulb air temperature or moisture), while positive values correspond to a heat gain due to an increase in temperature or increased relative humidity. The sum of all negative Space_load values was calculated as Space_load_loss and of 18 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. the sum of all positive Space_load values was calculated as Space_load_gain to account for the separate losses and gains, respectively. The same was done for Misc_load_loss and Misc_load_gain. There can be either gains or losses during day and nighttime periods during the winter evaluation. During the winter, air infiltration introduces air from the outside with lower temperature and moisture content into the building, so the space air is cooled and dehumidified naturally. In addition, significant heat flows occur from the building to the outside air due to heat transfer through the envelope, further reducing the indoor air temperature. A negative value of the Misc_load (or ventilation load) indicates that the enthalpy of mixed air compared to return air is reduced due to mixing of the cold and dry outside air.
